findings.title: Sweep completion may match a stale earlier operation
findings.message: For the second and third sweeps, polling stops as soon as the last recorded operation is completed. If the newly started operation is not yet appended, the previous sweep's completed operation and result are used. This gives spurious shape failures or validates the wrong data.
findings.suggestion: Record `len(Operations)` or the operation ID returned by `sweep.start`. Wait until that specific operation, or an operations count of `iteration+1`, reaches completed.

findings.title: Possible nil/out-of-range panic on noise result
findings.message: `result.Noise` and `OutputRMS` are dereferenced and indexed without checks. A malformed or partial noise result would panic the conformance run instead of returning an error. The same applies to `point.Values[0]` above.
findings.suggestion: Before indexing, check that `result.Noise != nil` and `len(result.Noise.OutputRMS) > 0`, and that `len(point.Values) > 0`. Return an error when any of these is missing.

findings.title: Nil DCSweep dereference / vacuous check after edit
findings.message: After `component.set`, `state.DCSweep` is dereferenced without a nil check, so the test panics if it is nil. If `Operations` is empty, the source-association check passes vacuously, even though captures were expected to survive the reload.
findings.suggestion: Require that `state.DCSweep` is non-nil and has the expected number of operations before iterating over them.

findings.title: Nil slice used as 'reference not set' sentinel
findings.message: The reference uses a nil-slice sentinel. If the first adapter returns a nil or empty result without an error, the next adapter becomes the reference instead, so the cross-adapter comparison silently loses its baseline. The pointer-based suites do not have this problem.
findings.suggestion: Track the reference with a separate `boundaryReferenceSet bool`, or treat an empty result as a failure.

findings.title: Unchecked index into Operations can panic
findings.message: The test indexes `state.DCSweep.Operations[0]` without checking the length. If the edit clears or never records operations, the test panics instead of failing with a clear message. It also ignores whether R1 was found.
findings.suggestion: Check that the component was found and that Operations is non-empty before indexing.

findings.title: 1ms busy polling of project.inspect
findings.message: The status loop polls `project.inspect` every 1ms for up to 35s per sweep. Over the socket transport this hammers the server and can record tens of thousands of commands in `s.commands`, which inflates memory and the result JSON.
findings.suggestion: Use a larger poll interval (e.g. 10–50ms), or a server-side wait/notification if one is available.

findings.title: Parity comparison never exercised across modes
findings.message: The test only compares each mode's results against themselves, so the parity check between in-process and socket is never exercised. The negative tests also only cover a missing case and missing commands, not noise or action divergence.
findings.suggestion: Collect results from both modes and call `CompareAnalysisBoundaries(inProcess, socket)`. Also add negative cases that perturb `NoiseRMS` or the command order.
